root_idea.summary: The root centers on weaving or interlacing into a close, firm structure.
root_idea.development: From weaving armor, the sense extends to any tightly woven or intricately interlaced workmanship, including the Quranic description of woven couches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized passive-participle citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the feminine form describes the couches of Paradise in 56:15; the contextual rendering “decorated” reflects their elaborate woven workmanship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A girth or harness strap, especially a broad strap woven from thongs or hair, or made of skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as equipment fitted to a saddle or howdah, with related saddle-harness terminology distinguishing its particular application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A basket or container, identified with a marjūnah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Classical Arabic noun for a type of basket or container.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Its woven-workmanship and girth meanings are represented.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the feminine inflected form مَوْضُونَةٍ; the public headword is normalized to the masculine singular passive-participle citation form مَوْضُونٌ.
The English gloss “decorated” is contextual support for the Quranic woven-workmanship sense, not a separate lexical sense.
